blocks.content:
Judges of High Courts are appointed by the President.

The President consults:
• Chief Justice of India
• Governor of the State
• Chief Justice of the High Court (in case of other judges)

The Collegium System plays an important role in recommendations.
Judges of High Courts are appointed by the President.

items: Remember that High Court judges are appointed by the President, NOT the Governor of the State.
Article 217 specifically governs the appointment and conditions of the office of a High Court Judge.
Consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court is required specifically when appointing 'other judges' of that court.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: High Court Judges are formally appointed by the President of India under Article 217.
The President must consult the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the concerned State.
When appointing other judges of a High Court, the Chief Justice of that High Court is also consulted.
The Collegium System holds a crucial role in recommending suitable candidates for appointment.
